Put one absolutely positioned pill (accent gradient, radius 999px) behind the tab row, exactly one tab wide: width: calc((100% - padding) / 4). prompt: Build a bottom tab bar with a curved notch that slides under the active tab, and a raised circle that carries the active icon inside the notch. Make the bar a full-width element pinned to the bottom (padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). Draw its background as an inline SVG path in an element with filter: drop-shadow(...) so the shadow follows the cut: M0 0 H(x - hw) A R R 0 1 0 (x + hw) 0 H width V height H0 Z, where x is the center of the active tab, R is the notch radius (circle radius plus 4px gap) and hw = sqrt(R^2 - cy^2) for a circle center cy px below the top edge. Animate x with a small spring integrator in requestAnimationFrame (v += (target - x) * .2; v *= .74; x += v) and update the path d attribute and the circle transform: translateX(x) together each frame, so cut and circle never drift apart. The circle is accent gradient, about 48px, sticking 18px above the bar, and its icon crossfades with a small scale. The active tab's own icon fades and drops 8px while its label stays visible below the notch. Tabs are real buttons in a nav with aria-current="page", 44px hit areas, focus-visible rings. prompt: Build a bottom tab bar that slides away when the user scrolls down and returns the moment they scroll up. Keep the bar pinned (position: sticky or fixed at the bottom with env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) and listen for scroll on the real scroller with a passive listener. Track the last scrollTop: if the delta is greater than 4px downward and scrollTop is past 12px, add a hidden class; if the delta is greater than 4px upward, or scrollTop is under 12px, remove it. Only update the stored position when the delta passes the 4px threshold so tiny jitters and rubber banding do not flicker the bar. The hidden state is transform: translateY(calc(100% + 24px)) with a 500ms cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) transition, never top or bottom. Keep the bar reachable: show it again on focus-within, when the page reaches the bottom, and when the user taps near the bottom edge. Do not hide it while a tab menu or sheet is open. Under prefers-reduced-motion use a 150ms opacity fade instead of the slide. Use a nav element with aria-current="page", 44px hit areas and visible focus rings. Plain HTML, CSS and a few lines of JS, no libraries.

prompt: Build horizontally swipeable pages with a bottom tab indicator that follows the scroll position continuously, not only when the swipe settles. Make the pages a flex row inside one scroller: overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; each page flex: none; width: 100%; scroll-snap-align: start; hide the scrollbar and set overscroll-behavior: contain. On the scroller's scroll event (passive, throttled to requestAnimationFrame) compute progress = scrollLeft / clientWidth and set the indicator pill, which is one tab wide, to transform: translateX(progress * 100%) scaleX(1 + .3 * sin(PI * fractionalPart)), so it stretches between tabs while the finger is still down and relaxes when the page snaps. Set the current tab styling from Math.round(progress). Tapping a tab calls scroller.scrollTo({ left: index * clientWidth, behavior: 'smooth' }), so the same code path animates the indicator. Never write left or width to move the pill. Use role="tablist" with role="tab" and aria-selected, tabpanels for the pages with only the visible one exposed, arrow keys to move between tabs, 44px hit areas and focus rings. Suppress the click that follows the release (capture phase, stopImmediatePropagation) so the hold does not also navigate. Add a light haptic where available (navigator.vibrate(8)), put a translucent scrim under the popover that closes it on tap, and list accounts as menuitems with the active one checked; picking one swaps the avatar and closes the menu. Also open it with a context menu event and Shift+F10 / the Menu key for keyboard and mouse users, set aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded on the tab, trap and restore focus, and disable the native touch callout with -webkit-touch-callout: none. Under prefers-reduced-motion fade the popover. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

prompt: Build a bottom navigation made of two floating pieces: a tabs pill and a separate round compose button, with the selection shown as a soft glass lens. Lay them out at the bottom with 10px gaps (pill: calc(100% - compose size - gaps), 56px tall, radius 999px, a light tinted background with a hairline inset ring; compose: 56px circle in your accent gradient). Inside the pill put one lens element behind the tab row, exactly one tab wide: a near-white vertical gradient (white to 62% white), an inset 1px white ring, an inset top highlight and a soft outer shadow so it reads as a thin piece of glass. Move it with transform only: on change, translateX(index * 100%) scale(1.16, 1.1) over 200ms cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) (the lens swells as it travels), then 170ms later settle to scale(1) on a slight-overshoot spring such as 594ms linear(0, 0.083 5.6%, 0.26 11.1%, 0.457 16.7%, 0.633 22.2%, 0.774 27.8%, 0.876 33.3%, 0.944 38.9%, 0.986 44.4%, 1.008 50%, 1.018 55.6%, 1.02 61.1%, 1.018 66.7%, 1.014 72.2%, 1 100%). Do not use backdrop-filter over scrolling content, a static tinted fill is enough and cheaper. The compose button scales to .9 on :active in 90ms and springs back. Use role="tablist" in the pill, aria-current or aria-selected on tabs, a labelled compose button, 44px hit areas, focus rings, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) spacing. Under prefers-reduced-motion skip the swell. Plain HTML, CSS and a few lines of JS, no libraries.

Fade the new label in over 300ms after an 80ms delay. Active icon and label are ink on the white chip, others are white at 55%. prompt: Build the "tap the active tab again" behavior: re-selecting the current tab scrolls its content back to the top and refreshes it, and the tab icon tells the user that is what will happen. Keep one real scroller for the page. A click on a tab that is already current calls reselect(): add an up class to the tab, call scroller.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' }), then about 480ms later show a small pill ("Updating", with a shimmer bar built from a moving background-position gradient, never a circular spinner) that drops in with transform: translateY on a critically damped spring such as 587ms linear(0, 0.094 5.6%, 0.274 11.1%, 0.455 16.7%, 0.608 22.2%, 0.726 27.8%, 0.812 33.3%, 0.873 38.9%, 0.916 44.4%, 0.944 50%, 0.964 55.6%, 0.976 61.1%, 0.985 66.7%, 0.99 72.2%, 1 100%), then fetch new items, insert them at the top, hide the pill and remove the up class. The icon swap is two stacked SVGs in one grid cell: the house fades out moving up 7px at scale .6 while the arrow-up fades in from below on a slight-overshoot spring (594ms linear(0, 0.083 5.6%, 0.26 11.1%, 0.457 16.7%, 0.633 22.2%, 0.774 27.8%, 0.876 33.3%, 0.944 38.9%, 0.986 44.4%, 1.008 50%, 1.018 55.6%, 1.02 61.1%, 1.018 66.7%, 1.014 72.2%, 1 100%)), and the label crossfades from Home to Top. If the user is already at the top, skip the scroll and only refresh. Debounce repeated taps, clear pending timers on a new tap, and announce "Feed updated" through a polite live region. Use a nav with aria-current="page", 44px hit areas and visible focus rings. Under prefers-reduced-motion jump to the top with behavior: 'auto'. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.

prompt: Build a bottom tab bar with a More tab that opens a sheet containing a grid of extra destinations, where picking one swaps it into the bar. The bar has five buttons: four destinations and More (aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing at the sheet). The sheet is a floating white card above the bar (radius 29px, grabber, title, a 4 by 2 grid of 54px rounded tiles with an icon and a label) that slides in with transform: translateY(130%) to none on a critically damped spring such as 587ms linear(0, 0.094 5.6%, 0.274 11.1%, 0.455 16.7%, 0.608 22.2%, 0.726 27.8%, 0.812 33.3%, 0.873 38.9%, 0.916 44.4%, 0.944 50%, 0.964 55.6%, 0.976 61.1%, 0.985 66.7%, 0.99 72.2%, 1 100%), with a 70% white scrim under it that closes it on tap. Tiles are tabbable only while open, Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to More. Picking a tile does three things: store the chosen destination as the fourth slot in your data (persist it so the bar remembers it), replace the fourth button's icon and label with the tile's, and play a short pop (scale .5 to 1.15 to 1 with opacity, 500ms) on the new content, then close the sheet and show that destination's page with the same directional crossfade the other tabs use. Tapping the fourth button again goes to the swapped destination. Only transform and opacity animate. Use a nav with aria-current="page", 44px hit areas, focus rings, role="dialog" on the sheet and inert on the page behind while open. Under prefers-reduced-motion fade the sheet. Plain HTML, CSS and JS, no libraries.
